actionability.justification: The rule specifies a concrete behavior change (run declared checks, report actual results, never say done/complete while a check fails) rather than a vague aspiration, though it doesn't specify what to do next after reporting a failure.

generality_without_vagueness.justification: Broadening 'release' to 'task, fix, migration, or release' generalizes the rule to the whole completion-claim failure class while keeping the concrete verify-then-report mechanism, avoiding platitude territory.

leakage.justification: The remedy text uses only generic terms (task, fix, migration, release, declared verification/test checks) with no project-specific nouns, tool names, or incident-specific details.

routing_fitness.justification: Revising the existing R2 claude-md rule to widen its scope is the cheapest adequate fix given R2 already implements this exact verify-before-claim mechanism, correctly avoiding a redundant new skill (R1) or a new sibling rule.

trigger_quality.justification: As a claude-md rule (not a skill) it has no formal 'Use when ...' trigger; the heading and opening clause ('Before reporting ... as complete') function as an implicit trigger but are less precise than a dedicated trigger clause.
